summary: Scientists and analysts who would watch the stratosphere and lower atmosphere for solar radiation modification (SRM). That covers sanctioned outdoor experiments, such as those funded under the UK ARIA climate-cooling programme, unilateral or rogue releases like Make Sunsets' balloon launches, and natural analogues such as volcanic eruptions. They detect and attribute aerosol signals, check claims against observations and brief governments and the public under a governance regime that is still forming. AI helps most with fusing data from satellites, lidar and reanalysis, writing up attribution uncertainty, keeping track of a patchy regulatory picture and explaining contested science in plain language.

prompts.title: Daily stratospheric aerosol watch summary
prompts.task: Turn overnight observations into a triaged watch report
prompts.prompt: You are assisting a stratospheric aerosol monitoring analyst. Below are the past [TIME WINDOW] of observations: [PASTE OMPS-LP / SAGE III-ISS extinction anomalies, ground lidar (e.g. NDACC) profiles, SO2 retrievals, and known volcanic/wildfire events from VAAC or FIRMS]. Produce a watch report with: (1) a table of anomalies (location, altitude, magnitude vs. climatology, data source); (2) for each, the most likely natural explanation and how confident that is; (3) which anomalies are not explained by known volcanic, pyroCb or rocket-exhaust sources and need a follow-up; (4) suggested next observations. Flag data gaps and retrieval artifacts explicitly. Do not label anything a deliberate release.
prompts.caution: Attribution to a deliberate release is a human expert call that needs corroboration; treat AI triage as a starting point only.

prompts.title: Attribution uncertainty memo
prompts.task: Assess whether a detected signal could be an intentional release
prompts.prompt: Act as a skeptical atmospheric scientist reviewing an attribution question. Signal: [DESCRIBE DETECTION: species, altitude, plume extent, timing, location]. Candidate sources: [LIST, e.g. volcanic degassing, pyroCb smoke, aviation, a claimed balloon release by NAMED ACTOR, instrument error]. Write a 1-2 page memo that: weighs the evidence for and against each source; lists which further data (trajectory modeling with HYSPLIT or FLEXPART, isotopic or composition sampling, satellite overpasses, flight records) would discriminate between them; and states a calibrated confidence using IPCC-style likelihood language. End with open questions and what would change the conclusion.
prompts.caution: Public accusations of deliberate deployment have diplomatic consequences; route conclusions through institutional review.

prompts.title: Verifying a startup's cooling claims
prompts.task: Check claims of sold 'cooling credits' from small SO2 releases
prompts.prompt: I monitor commercial solar geoengineering claims. A company, [COMPANY], says it released [MASS] of [SO2/OTHER] via [METHOD, e.g. weather balloon] at [ALTITUDE/LOCATION/DATE] and sells credits claiming [STATED COOLING, e.g. tonne-years of CO2 offset]. Evaluate the claim: estimate whether such a release is detectable with current instruments; review the physical assumptions behind the cooling-equivalence figure, such as aerosol lifetime, radiative forcing efficiency and whether the payload reached the stratosphere; and list the evidence the company would need to publish to substantiate it. Output a claim-by-claim table (claim, assessment, evidence needed) and a short summary. Separate established physics from contested estimates.
prompts.caution: Stay factual and evidence-based; this may inform regulators (e.g. Mexico's 2023 ban response) or consumer-protection actions.

prompts.title: Governance and regulation tracker
prompts.task: Map the legal status of SRM activity across jurisdictions
prompts.prompt: You are a policy research assistant for a geoengineering monitoring team. Build a structured brief on the current governance of outdoor solar radiation modification relevant to [JURISDICTIONS / ACTIVITY TYPE, e.g. stratospheric balloon releases, marine cloud brightening]. Cover: the CBD decision X/33 and later COP decisions; the ENMOD Convention; the London Convention/Protocol marine geoengineering amendments; US NOAA weather-modification reporting under 15 CFR Part 908; state-level bans (e.g. Tennessee, Florida); Mexico's 2023 position; and any UNEP or UNEA activity. For each: what it covers, whether it is binding, and its status. Mark anything you are unsure is current and tell me to verify it against primary sources as of [DATE].
prompts.caution: Governance is changing fast and Claude's knowledge has a cutoff; verify every item against primary texts before relying on it.

prompts.title: Public explainer after a detection
prompts.task: Communicate a monitoring finding without hype or conspiracy fuel
prompts.prompt: Help me write a public statement for [ORGANIZATION] about [EVENT, e.g. a detected stratospheric aerosol anomaly / a confirmed small release by a named group]. Audience: the general public and journalists, many of whom have seen 'chemtrail' claims. Write about 300 words in plain English that: say what was observed and what was not; give the scale compared with familiar references such as a volcanic eruption or annual aviation emissions; say honestly what is still unknown; explain why contrails are not geoengineering; and say where people can see the data. Then give 5 likely press questions with suggested answers. Avoid alarmism and false reassurance alike.
prompts.caution: Have scientific and comms leads sign off; never overstate certainty about intent or health effects.

prompts.title: Monitoring plan for a sanctioned field experiment
prompts.task: Design an independent observation plan for an authorized outdoor test
prompts.prompt: Act as an independent monitoring lead for an authorized small-scale outdoor SRM experiment: [DESCRIBE: e.g. marine cloud brightening spray trial / stratospheric balloon release, scale, location, funder such as an ARIA-funded project, dates]. Draft a monitoring plan with: objectives; baseline measurements before release; the instruments and platforms to use during and after release, with justification; detection thresholds and how likely the signal is to be detectable at this scale; stop or abort criteria tied to environmental indicators; data-sharing and open-publication commitments; and community-notification steps. Format as a numbered plan with a summary table. Flag assumptions that need site-specific validation.
prompts.caution: This is oversight planning for permitted research; final protocols need ethics review, permits and local consultation.

prompts.title: Termination-shock and scenario briefing
prompts.task: Brief decision-makers on long-term SRM risk scenarios
prompts.prompt: I need a briefing for [AUDIENCE, e.g. a national climate security office] on risk scenarios a geoengineering monitoring service should be ready for over the next 10-20 years. Using GeoMIP/CMIP studies, the 2023 UNEP 'One Atmosphere' review and the US National Academies 2021 report as anchors, summarize: unilateral deployment by a state or private actor; termination shock; regional precipitation and monsoon effects; ozone impacts; and moral-hazard effects on emissions policy. For each, give the indicators monitors would watch, lead times and the main scientific uncertainties. Use a table plus a 200-word executive summary. Flag where model results disagree.
prompts.caution: Model projections are uncertain; present ranges, not point predictions, and cite sources the reader can check.

prompts.title: Upskilling study plan
prompts.task: Build a learning path into stratospheric monitoring
prompts.prompt: I'm moving into solar geoengineering monitoring from [BACKGROUND, e.g. air-quality science / satellite remote sensing / climate policy]. Design a [DURATION] self-study plan covering: stratospheric chemistry and aerosol microphysics; radiative forcing basics; satellite limb and lidar retrievals (OMPS-LP, SAGE III, CALIPSO archive); trajectory modeling (HYSPLIT); volcanic analogues such as Pinatubo and Hunga Tonga; and SRM governance and ethics. For each week give learning goals, specific readings or courses, a hands-on exercise using public data (e.g. NASA Earthdata, MERRA-2) and a self-check question. Point out where the field is unsettled and which skills transfer from my background.
